reference: HRSA 340B Drug Pricing Program; CMS Part D 340B Duplicate Discount Policy

description: Indicates whether this claim is for a compounded drug product containing multiple ingredients (True = compound claim). Compound claims require line-level detail in the pharmacy_claim_line product. Used for compound drug utilization review and cost management.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Compound Segment; CMS Part D Compound Drug Rules

description: Line of business under which this pharmacy claim was adjudicated. Drives regulatory reporting requirements, formulary rules, and cost-sharing structures. 'commercial' = employer-sponsored or individual; 'medicare_part_d' = CMS Medicare Part D; 'medicaid' = state Medicaid; 'exchange' = ACA marketplace QHP; 'cobra' = COBRA continuation coverage.
reference: CMS Part D; ACA QHP Standards; NAIC LOB Reporting; ERISA

description: Percentage-based cost-sharing amount paid by the member for this pharmacy claim, calculated as a percentage of the allowed cost. Applies when the benefit design uses coinsurance rather than fixed copay. Contributes to OOP/MOOP accumulation.
reference: NCPDP D.0; ACA Cost-Sharing Rules; CMS Part D Benefit Design

description: Fixed dollar amount paid by the member at point of sale as their cost-sharing obligation for this pharmacy claim. Determined by formulary tier and benefit design. Contributes to member out-of-pocket (OOP) and maximum out-of-pocket (MOOP) accumulation.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Field 506-F6; ACA MOOP Limits; CMS Part D Cost-Sharing Rules

description: 11-digit National Drug Code identifying the specific drug product dispensed, including labeler, product, and package segment. Denormalized from the drug master for claim-level auditability and CMS Part D encounter data submission (EDPS). Required for 340B duplicate discount prevention and drug utilization review (DUR).
reference: FDA NDC Directory; NCPDP D.0 Field 407-D7; CMS Part D EDPS

description: Claim number of the original pharmacy claim that this record adjusts or reverses. Populated only for adjusted or reversed claims; null for original claims. Enables claim adjustment chain tracing for financial reconciliation, audit, and CMS Part D encounter data correction submissions.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Claim Adjustment; CMS Part D EDPS Adjustment Processing; HIPAA 835

description: Channel through which the drug was dispensed. Drives cost-sharing differentials, formulary tier rules, and network adequacy reporting. 'retail' = community pharmacy; 'mail_order' = 90-day mail service; 'specialty' = specialty pharmacy for high-cost/complex drugs; 'long_term_care' = SNF/LTC pharmacy; 'home_infusion' = infusion therapy at home.
reference: CMS Part D Pharmacy Type Codes; NCPDP D.0 Pharmacy Service Type

description: Total amount paid by the health plan for this pharmacy claim after applying member cost-sharing (copay, coinsurance, deductible) and COB adjustments. Net total component of the MONETARY_TRIPLET. Used for 835 remittance, MLR reporting, and CMS Part D encounter data.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Field 505-F5; HIPAA 835 Remittance; CMS Part D EDPS

description: 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the prescribing provider as submitted on the pharmacy claim. Denormalized for claim-level auditability, NCPDP D.0 compliance, and CMS Part D encounter data submission. Used for prescriber fraud/waste/abuse (FWA) analytics.
reference: HIPAA NPI Final Rule 45 CFR §162.406; NCPDP D.0 Field 411-DB; CMS NPI Registry

description: Date the prescription was written by the prescriber. Used to validate prescription age, enforce days-supply-from-written-date rules, and support medication adherence analytics. Distinct from fill_date (dispensing date).
reference: NCPDP D.0 Field 414-DE (Date Prescription Written); State Pharmacy Board Regulations

description: Actual quantity of the drug dispensed (e.g., number of tablets, milliliters, grams) as reported by the dispensing pharmacy. Used for quantity limit (QL) edits, drug utilization review (DUR), and CMS Part D encounter data submission.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Field 442-E7; CMS Part D EDPS Quantity Dispensed

description: NCPDP standard unit of measure code for the quantity dispensed. EA = each (tablets/capsules); ML = milliliters; GM = grams; UN = units; F2 = international units; ME = milliequivalents. Required for accurate quantity limit (QL) edit enforcement and CMS Part D encounter data.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Field 600-28 (Unit of Measure); CMS Part D EDPS

description: Refill sequence number for this dispensing event. Zero (0) indicates the original fill; subsequent values indicate refill number. Used for refill-too-soon edits, medication adherence tracking, and prescription lifecycle management.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Field 403-D3; CMS Part D Refill Rules

description: NCPDP standard reject code returned by the PBM system when a claim is rejected or denied. Null for paid claims. Used for pharmacy operations, member appeals, and drug utilization review (DUR) outcome tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product — NCPDP reject codes exceed 6 values]
reference: NCPDP D.0 Reject Code List; CMS Part D Reject Code Requirements

description: Sales tax amount applied to the pharmacy claim where applicable by state law. Included in total claim cost and reported separately for financial reconciliation and statutory accounting (SAP) purposes.
reference: NCPDP D.0 Field 481-HA; State Tax Regulations

description: Indicates whether a step therapy protocol was overridden for this claim (True = override applied). Step therapy requires trying lower-cost drugs before approving higher-cost alternatives. Override requires prior authorization. Used for utilization management (UM) reporting and CMS step therapy compliance.
reference: CMS Step Therapy Rule (42 CFR §422.136); NCQA UM Standards

description: Timestamp when this pharmacy claim record was last modified in the Silver layer, such as after a claim adjustment, reversal, or COB update. Supports change data capture (CDC) and audit trail requirements. RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.312; Internal Data Governance Policy

description: Primary key for prior_authorization

Foreign key linking to utilization.clinical_criteria. Business justification: Pharmacy PA decisions are evaluated against specific clinical criteria sets (e.g., MCG drug criteria, InterQual). Regulatory audits and URAC accreditation require documenting which clinical criteria v

Foreign key linking to care.condition_registry. Business justification: PA requests are clinically grounded in a member's registered chronic condition (e.g., oncology drug PA tied to cancer in condition registry). Proper FK replaces denormalized icd_diagnosis_code, enable

Foreign key linking to pharmacy.drug_master. Business justification: A prior authorization is issued for a specific drug identified by NDC. The drug_ndc STRING on prior_authorization should be normalized to a FK referencing the authoritative drug_master record. This en
Identifier of the formulary associated with the member's plan at the time of the prior authorization request. Determines drug tier, coverage rules, and applicable PA criteria.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; PBM Formulary Management (RxClaim/Argus)

description: Foreign key linking to risk.member_risk_score. Business justification: Prior‑authorization workflow uses the member's risk score to assess clinical necessity and cost containment, mandated by internal utilization management policies.
Reference to the original prior authorization record when this record represents a renewal, appeal, or modification. Enables tracking of the full PA lifecycle chain. Null for initial requests.
reference: CMS Part D PA Continuity; URAC UM Standards

description: Foreign key linking to utilization.pa_request. Business justification: Required for PA audit report linking each prior authorization record to its originating request, enabling traceability of request‑to‑authorization lifecycle.

Foreign key linking to provider.provider. Business justification: PA requests are submitted by prescribing providers. Linking PA to provider.provider enables credentialing/network status validation at PA adjudication, prescriber-level PA reporting, and regulatory co
Indicates whether this prior authorization record is associated with a member or prescriber appeal of a prior denial. True = this PA is an appeal case.
reference: CMS Part D Appeals and Grievances Requirements; URAC UM Standards; State DOI Appeal Regulations

description: Number of days of drug therapy authorized under this prior authorization. Used by the PBM to enforce dispensing limits and by CMS Part D for compliance reporting.
reference: CMS Part D Days Supply Rules; NCPDP Telecommunication Standard

description: Total quantity of the drug authorized for dispensing under this prior authorization (e.g., number of tablets, milliliters, units). Enforced at point-of-sale by the PBM adjudication system.
reference: CMS Part D Quantity Limit Rules; NCPDP Telecommunication Standard

description: Number of refills authorized under this prior authorization in addition to the initial fill. Enforced by the PBM adjudication system at point-of-sale.
reference: CMS Part D; NCPDP Telecommunication Standard; DEA Controlled Substance Regulations

description: Version of the clinical criteria set (InterQual or MCG) applied at the time of the prior authorization decision. Required for audit trails and appeals to ensure the correct criteria version is referenced.
reference: InterQual Clinical Criteria; MCG Care Guidelines; URAC UM Accreditation

business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Part D Reportable Indicator
description: Indicates whether this prior authorization record is subject to CMS Part D PA reporting requirements. True = must be included in CMS Part D PA reporting submissions.
reference: CMS Part D Prior Authorization Reporting Requirements; 42 CFR §423

description: Timestamp when this prior authorization record was first created in the Silver Layer data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer processing compliance.
reference: HIPAA Audit Controls 45 CFR §164.312; Enterprise Data Governance; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: Indicates whether the submitted clinical information met the applicable clinical criteria (InterQual/MCG) for the requested drug. True = criteria met (supports approval); False = criteria not met (supports denial).
reference: InterQual Clinical Criteria; MCG Care Guidelines; CMS Part D PA Requirements

description: Exact date and time the prior authorization decision (approval, denial, or pend) was rendered by the clinical reviewer or automated adjudication engine. Used to calculate turnaround time against CMS and URAC standards.
reference: CMS Part D PA Timeliness Standards; URAC UM Accreditation; NCQA Accreditation

description: Standardized code indicating the reason for denial of the prior authorization request (e.g., not medically necessary, step therapy not completed, quantity limit exceeded, non-covered drug). Populated only when pa_status = denied. Used for member appeals and CMS Part D reporting.
reference: CMS Part D Denial Reason Codes; NCPDP Reject Codes; URAC UM Standards

description: Free-text description of the denial reason, providing clinical or administrative context beyond the denial reason code. Included in member and prescriber denial notices per CMS and state DOI requirements.
reference: CMS Part D Denial Notice Requirements; State DOI Adverse Determination Notice Rules; URAC UM Standards

description: Pharmacy dispensing channel authorized for this prior authorization (retail, mail-order, specialty pharmacy, long-term care, or home infusion). Determines which pharmacy network is eligible to dispense.
reference: CMS Part D Pharmacy Network Requirements; NCPDP Pharmacy Type Codes; PBM Network Management

description: Formulary tier of the requested drug at the time of the prior authorization request. Determines cost-sharing obligations and PA criteria applied.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Tier Requirements; PBM Formulary Management (RxClaim/Argus)

description: NCPDP-standardized Drug Utilization Review (DUR) outcome code resulting from prospective DUR screening performed during PA adjudication (e.g., drug-drug interaction, drug-disease contraindication, duplicate therapy). Sourced from PBM system (RxClaim/Argus).
reference: NCPDP DUR Standard; CMS Part D DUR Requirements; OBRA 1990 DUR Mandate

description: Date on which the prior authorization expires and is no longer valid for dispensing. After this date, a new PA request is required. Nullable for open-ended authorizations.
reference: CMS Part D; NCPDP Telecommunication Standard; PBM Adjudication Rules

description: Date from which the approved prior authorization is valid for dispensing. Pharmacies and PBM adjudication systems use this date to confirm dispensing eligibility.
reference: CMS Part D; NCPDP Telecommunication Standard; PBM Adjudication Rules

description: Line of Business (LOB) under which the member's coverage falls, determining applicable regulatory requirements, formulary rules, and PA criteria (e.g., Commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid, ACA Marketplace).
reference: CMS Part D; ACA Qualified Health Plan (QHP); NAIC Model Laws; State DOI Regulations

description: Free-text clinical notes entered by the reviewing clinician during the prior authorization evaluation, capturing clinical rationale, additional context, or instructions for the prescriber or pharmacy. Contains Protected Health Information (PHI).
reference: HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR §164; CMS Part D PA Documentation Requirements; URAC UM Standards

description: Externally-known, human-readable prior authorization reference number assigned by the Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) system (RxClaim or Argus) or Utilization Management (UM) system (InterQual/MCG). Used on Explanation of Benefits (EOB) and communicated to prescribers and pharmacies.
reference: CMS Part D; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; HIPAA 278 Transaction

description: Current lifecycle status of the prior authorization request. Drives dispensing eligibility at the pharmacy and CMS Part D PA reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: approved|denied|pending|cancelled|expired|appealed — promote to reference product if additional statuses are needed]
reference: CMS Part D Prior Authorization; NCPDP Telecommunication Standard; HIPAA 278 Transaction

description: Category of prior authorization criteria applied, indicating the clinical or formulary reason the drug requires PA review (e.g., specialty drug, non-preferred tier, step therapy requirement, quantity limit, age restriction, off-label use). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: specialty|non_preferred|step_therapy|quantity_limit|age_restriction|off_label — promote to reference product]
reference: CMS Part D Formulary and PA Requirements; PBM Formulary Management

description: Indicates whether a quantity limit restriction was a factor in the prior authorization evaluation. True = quantity limit rules were applied during adjudication.
reference: CMS Part D Quantity Limit Requirements; PBM Formulary Management (RxClaim/Argus)

description: Exact date and time the prior authorization request was received by the Utilization Management (UM) system (InterQual/MCG) or PBM system (RxClaim/Argus). Used for precise turnaround time calculation and regulatory compliance.
reference: CMS Part D PA Timeliness; URAC UM Accreditation Standards

description: Calendar date on which the prior authorization request was submitted by the prescriber or pharmacy. Used for turnaround time measurement and CMS Part D compliance reporting.
reference: CMS Part D PA Timeliness Standards; URAC Drug Therapy Management Standards

description: Classification of the prior authorization request indicating whether it is a new request, renewal of an existing authorization, appeal of a denial, expedited urgent request, or retrospective review.
reference: CMS Part D PA Requirements; URAC UM Standards; NCQA Accreditation

description: Level of clinical review applied to the prior authorization request, indicating whether it was reviewed by a pharmacist, physician, peer-to-peer consultation, or medical director. Escalation level affects turnaround time standards.
reference: URAC UM Accreditation Standards; NCQA Accreditation; CMS Part D PA Requirements

description: Native prior authorization identifier from the originating operational system (RxClaim, Argus, InterQual, or MCG). Preserved for reconciliation, audit, and cross-system traceability in the Silver Layer.
reference: Enterprise Data Governance; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: Indicates whether the requested drug is classified as a specialty drug requiring specialty pharmacy dispensing and enhanced clinical review. Specialty drugs typically have higher cost-sharing and stricter PA criteria.
reference: CMS Part D Specialty Tier Definition; NCPDP Specialty Drug Classification; PBM Formulary Management

description: Indicates whether the member has documented evidence of completing the required step therapy (tried and failed prerequisite drugs) as required by the formulary PA criteria. Populated when step_therapy_required = True.
reference: CMS Part D Step Therapy Rules; NCQA Formulary Management Standards

description: Indicates whether the prior authorization requires the member to have tried and failed one or more preferred or lower-tier drugs (step therapy) before the requested drug is authorized. True = step therapy applies.
reference: CMS Part D Step Therapy Rules; NCQA Formulary Management Standards; State DOI Step Therapy Laws

description: Timestamp when this prior authorization record was last modified in the Silver Layer data platform, reflecting status changes, decision updates, or data corrections. Used for change data capture and audit.
reference: HIPAA Audit Controls 45 CFR §164.312; Enterprise Data Governance; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the dispensing pharmacy record within the PBM network master. Primary key for this entity.

Foreign key linking to billing.account. Business justification: Network dispensing pharmacies are reimbursed through a billing account for ingredient costs and dispensing fees. Pharmacy network payment operations require a billing account reference to process EFT

Internal pharmacy identifier assigned by the PBM system (RxClaim or Argus) for claim routing and adjudication. May differ from NCPDP ID in multi-PBM environments. Used for system-level reconciliation.
reference: RxClaim/Argus PBM System; NCPDP Claim Adjudication Standard

description: Foreign key linking to provider.facility. Business justification: Hospital outpatient pharmacies and specialty pharmacies embedded in facilities must be linked to provider.facility for network credentialing, directory accuracy, and network adequacy reporting. Regula

business_glossary_term: National Council for Prescription Drug Programs (NCPDP) Provider ID
description: The 7-digit NCPDP pharmacy identifier (formerly NABP number) used as the primary pharmacy identifier in PBM claim transactions, formulary lookups, and pharmacy network directories. Sourced from RxClaim or Argus PBM system.
reference: NCPDP Provider Identification Standard; CMS Part D; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 162

description: Foreign key linking to network.service_area. Business justification: CMS Part D and state Medicaid regulations require pharmacy network adequacy assessment by service area. Linking dispensing pharmacies to service areas enables geographic access reporting, regulatory f

Foreign key linking to network.par_agreement. Business justification: Dispensing pharmacies have formal participation agreements governing network inclusion terms, credentialing, and reimbursement. The PAR agreement is the authoritative record of a pharmacy's network pa

Foreign key linking to billing.payment_method. Business justification: Dispensing pharmacies must have a registered payment method (EFT/ACH bank account) for network reimbursement disbursements. Health insurance pharmacy network operations require payment method registra

Foreign key linking to care.program. Business justification: Specialty pharmacies are designated as preferred or exclusive dispensers for specific care management programs (e.g., oncology specialty pharmacy, transplant program, hemophilia program). This link en

Foreign key linking to network.provider_network. Business justification: Required for network participation reporting and CMS network adequacy; each pharmacy must be linked to the provider network it belongs to.

Foreign key linking to network.tier. Business justification: Pharmacy network tiering drives member cost-sharing — preferred vs. standard vs. specialty pharmacy tiers determine copay differentials. Benefit design and EOB generation require knowing which network

Indicates whether the pharmacy is enabled to receive electronic prescriptions (e-prescribing) via NCPDP SCRIPT standard. Required for controlled substance e-prescribing (EPCS) compliance in many states.
reference: NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; DEA EPCS Regulations 21 CFR Part 1311; State E-Prescribing Mandates

description: Primary street address of the pharmacy dispensing location. Used for member pharmacy locator, network directory, and regulatory reporting.
reference: NCPDP Provider Identification Standard; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 162

description: Secondary address information (suite, unit, floor) for the pharmacy dispensing location.

The contracted discount percentage applied to the AWP for brand drug ingredient cost reimbursement. For example, AWP minus 15% means awp_discount_percent = 15.00. Applies when ingredient_cost_basis is 'awp_discount'. Commercially sensitive contract term.
reference: CMS Part D Reimbursement Standards; AWP Industry Benchmark; PBM Contract Standards

description: Indicates whether the pharmacy is part of a chain organization (e.g., CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid) or operates as an independent pharmacy. Affects contract terms, reimbursement rates, and network tier assignment.
reference: NCPDP Pharmacy Chain/Independent Classification; PBM Contract Standards

description: Name of the parent chain organization if the pharmacy is a chain location (e.g., CVS Health, Walgreens Boots Alliance). Null for independent pharmacies. Used for chain-level contract management and performance reporting.
reference: NCPDP Chain Code Standard; PBM Contract Management

description: City of the pharmacy dispensing location. Used for geographic network analysis, member access reporting, and CMS Part D network adequacy compliance.
reference: NCPDP Provider Identification Standard; CMS Part D Network Adequacy Standards

description: Indicates whether the pharmacy holds cold chain certification for temperature-sensitive drug storage and shipping (e.g., biologics, insulin, vaccines). Required for specialty and mail-order pharmacies dispensing refrigerated or frozen medications.
reference: USP Chapter 1118; URAC Specialty Pharmacy Accreditation; CMS Part D Specialty Drug Standards

description: Date on which the pharmacy's network participation contract becomes effective. Used to validate claim eligibility by service date and for contract lifecycle management.
reference: CMS Part D Pharmacy Contract Requirements; PBM Contract Standards

description: Date on which the pharmacy's network participation contract ends or was terminated. Null for active open-ended contracts. Used for claim eligibility validation and network adequacy gap analysis.
reference: CMS Part D Pharmacy Contract Requirements; PBM Contract Standards

description: Indicates whether the pharmacy reimbursement contract is negotiated directly with the health plan (direct) or administered through the PBM intermediary (PBM-administered). Affects financial settlement, audit rights, and MAC list applicability.
reference: PBM Contract Standards; ERISA; CMS Part D Pharmacy Contract Requirements

description: Timestamp when the dispensing pharmacy record was first created in the PBM network master. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory record retention requirements.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; CMS Part D Record Retention Requirements; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: The contracted per-prescription dispensing fee paid to the pharmacy in addition to ingredient cost reimbursement. Expressed in USD. May vary by pharmacy type, drug type, or days supply. Commercially sensitive contract term.
reference: CMS Part D Dispensing Fee Standards; PBM Contract Standards; NCPDP Claim Adjudication

description: Two-letter USPS state code of the state in which the pharmacy is licensed to dispense. May differ from the physical address state for mail-order pharmacies licensed in multiple states. Used for state-level regulatory compliance and claim adjudication.
reference: State Board of Pharmacy Regulations; NABP; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 162

description: Trade name or DBA name under which the pharmacy operates if different from the legal business name. Used in member-facing directories and communications.
Fax number for the pharmacy dispensing location. Used for prior authorization transmissions, prescription transfers, and clinical communications.
reference: NCPDP Provider Identification Standard; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

description: The pricing benchmark used to calculate ingredient cost reimbursement for drug claims. AWP (Average Wholesale Price) discount is most common for brand drugs; MAC (Maximum Allowable Cost) applies to generics; WAC (Wholesale Acquisition Cost) and NADAC (National Average Drug Acquisition Cost) are alternative benchmarks. Sourced from PBM contract terms in RxClaim/Argus.
reference: CMS Part D Reimbursement Standards; NCPDP Claim Adjudication; MAC/AWP/WAC Industry Standards

description: The health insurance line of business for which this pharmacy network participation record applies. A pharmacy may have separate network records per LOB with different contract terms. Drives claim adjudication routing and formulary selection.
reference: CMS Part D; Medicaid Managed Care Regulations 42 CFR Part 438; ACA Exchange Requirements

description: Indicates whether the pharmacy is certified and operationally capable of fulfilling mail-order prescriptions (90-day supply, home delivery). Drives claim routing and member benefit design enforcement.
reference: CMS Part D Mail Order Pharmacy Requirements; URAC Mail Service Pharmacy Accreditation

business_glossary_term: National Council for Prescription Drug Programs (NCPDP) Chain Code
description: NCPDP-assigned 4-digit chain code identifying the pharmacy chain organization. Used for chain-level contract application and bulk reimbursement rate assignment in the PBM system.

Date on which the pharmacy's current network participation status became effective. Distinct from contract_effective_date; captures the most recent network status change date (e.g., reactivation after suspension).
reference: CMS Part D Pharmacy Network Requirements; PBM Contract Standards

description: Current status of the pharmacy's participation in the PBM network. Drives real-time claim adjudication eligibility checks in RxClaim/Argus. Active pharmacies are eligible to dispense covered drugs; inactive/terminated pharmacies are rejected at point-of-sale.
reference: CMS Part D Pharmacy Network Requirements; NCQA Pharmacy Accreditation; PBM Contract Standards

description: Date on which the pharmacy's network participation was or is scheduled to be terminated. Null for currently active network participants. Used for claim eligibility validation and network adequacy gap analysis.
reference: CMS Part D Pharmacy Network Requirements; PBM Contract Standards

description: Indicates whether the pharmacy contract includes audit provisions allowing the PBM or health plan to conduct on-site or desk audits of dispensing records, pricing, and compliance. Required for CMS Part D sponsor oversight obligations.
reference: CMS Part D Audit Requirements 42 CFR Part 423; PBM Contract Standards; ERISA

description: Legal business name of the dispensing pharmacy as registered with the state board of pharmacy and NCPDP. Used in member-facing communications, EOB documents, and provider directory.
reference: NCPDP Provider Identification Standard; State Board of Pharmacy

description: Classification of the pharmacy by dispensing channel and operational model. Drives claim routing, reimbursement logic, and formulary applicability within the PBM system (RxClaim/Argus). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: retail|mail_order|specialty|long_term_care|compounding — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
reference: NCPDP Pharmacy Type Codes; CMS Part D Pharmacy Type Classification; PBM Industry Standard

description: Primary telephone number for the pharmacy dispensing location. Used for member contact, prior authorization coordination, and provider directory.

Indicates whether the pharmacy requires patient or authorized representative signature upon delivery for mail-order or specialty drug shipments. Relevant for controlled substances and high-value specialty medications.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; CMS Part D Delivery Requirements; NCPDP Claim Adjudication

description: Identifies the operational source system from which this pharmacy record was ingested (e.g., RxClaim, Argus PBM, Cactus credentialing system). Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation in the Databricks lakehouse Silver layer.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; Databricks Lakehouse Architecture

description: Accreditation body certification held by the pharmacy for specialty drug dispensing. URAC, ACHC, and NABP PCAB are the primary specialty pharmacy accreditation bodies recognized by health plans and PBMs. Required for specialty network participation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: urac|achc|jcaho|nabp_pcab|none — promote to reference product if multi-accreditation tracking is needed]
reference: URAC Specialty Pharmacy Accreditation Standards; ACHC Specialty Pharmacy Standards; NABP PCAB; CMS Part D Specialty Pharmacy Requirements

description: Two-letter USPS state abbreviation for the pharmacy dispensing location. Used for state-level licensure validation, network adequacy reporting, and regulatory compliance.
reference: USPS State Abbreviation Standard; NCPDP Provider Identification Standard; State DOI Regulations

description: Indicates whether the pharmacy operates 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. Used for network adequacy reporting and member access analysis, particularly for CMS Part D access requirements.
reference: CMS Part D Network Adequacy Standards; State DOI Network Adequacy Regulations

description: Timestamp when the dispensing pharmacy record was most recently updated. Used for change data capture, data quality monitoring, and audit trail in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; CMS Part D Record Retention Requirements; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: US ZIP or ZIP+4 postal code for the pharmacy dispensing location. Used for geographic network adequacy analysis, member proximity calculations, and CMS Part D access reporting.
reference: USPS ZIP Code Standard; CMS Part D Network Adequacy; NCPDP Provider Identification Standard

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each drug master record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Serves as the primary key for all downstream joins across formulary, claims, DUR, rebate contracting, and PBM adjudication.

The WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code at the 5th level, identifying the drug's anatomical main group, therapeutic subgroup, pharmacological subgroup, chemical subgroup, and chemical substance. Used for therapeutic class reporting, HEDIS pharmacy measures, population health analytics, and international drug classification alignment.
reference: WHO ATC/DDD Index; WHO Collaborating Centre for Drug Statistics Methodology; NCQA HEDIS Pharmacy Measures

description: The date on which the current AWP unit price became effective. Used to apply the correct AWP for historical claims repricing, audit reconciliation, and retroactive rebate calculations.
reference: First Databank AWP Update Schedule; Medi-Span AWP Update Schedule; CMS Part D Pricing

description: The Average Wholesale Price (AWP) per unit of the drug as published by First Databank or Medi-Span. AWP is the benchmark pricing reference used in pharmacy reimbursement calculations, MAC pricing comparisons, and rebate contract negotiations. Expressed in USD per unit (tablet, mL, gram, etc.).
reference: First Databank AWP; Medi-Span AWP; CMS Part D Pricing Benchmarks; NAIC Model Pharmacy Benefit Transparency Act

description: The proprietary trade name under which the drug is marketed by the manufacturer (e.g., Lipitor, Humira). Used in formulary tier assignment, rebate contracting, member communications, and brand vs. generic substitution logic in PBM adjudication.
reference: FDA Drug Labeling Requirements; First Databank Drug Database

description: The DEA controlled substance schedule classification (I through V) indicating the drug's potential for abuse and accepted medical use. Schedule II-V drugs require enhanced DUR edits, quantity limits, early refill restrictions, and special handling in PBM adjudication. Not_scheduled indicates no DEA restriction.
reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act (21 USC 812); DEA Schedule of Controlled Substances; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard

description: The timestamp when this drug master record was first created in the lakehouse Silver layer. Used for data lineage, audit compliance, and change data capture tracking per HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164.312); SOC 2 Audit Trail Requirements; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Indicates whether a valid DEA registration number is required on the prescription for this drug due to its controlled substance classification. Drives prescription validation edits in PBM adjudication and pharmacy dispensing workflows.
reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act (21 USC 829); DEA Practitioner Registration Requirements

description: The physical form in which the drug is dispensed (e.g., tablet, capsule, solution, injection, patch, inhaler). Critical for formulary configuration, quantity limit rules, step therapy protocols, and DUR screening in RxClaim/Argus. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|solution|injection|patch|inhaler|cream|ointment|suspension|powder — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA Dosage Form Terminology; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; First Databank Drug Database

description: The classification code for the drug class within the GPI or ETC hierarchy, representing a more granular grouping below therapeutic subclass (e.g., specific statin subtype). Used in formulary step therapy rules, DUR clinical edits, and rebate tier segmentation in PBM systems.
reference: First Databank Enhanced Therapeutic Classification (ETC); Medi-Span GPI Classification

description: The human-readable name of the drug class corresponding to the drug_class_code. Provides the most granular named classification level in the therapeutic hierarchy for formulary configuration and clinical reporting.
reference: First Databank Enhanced Therapeutic Classification (ETC); Medi-Span GPI Classification

description: The full proprietary or established name of the drug as it appears on the FDA-approved label and in the First Databank or Medi-Span drug database feed. Used as the primary human-readable identity label across formulary displays, EOB communications, and member-facing materials.
reference: FDA Drug Labeling Requirements; First Databank Drug Database; Medi-Span Drug Database

description: Current lifecycle status of the drug record in the master file. Active drugs are eligible for formulary placement and PBM adjudication. Discontinued or recalled drugs trigger claim edits and member/provider notifications. Drives formulary maintenance workflows in RxClaim/Argus.
reference: FDA Drug Approval and Market Status; First Databank Drug Database; CMS Part D Formulary Requirements

description: Classification of the drug as brand-name, generic, biosimilar, over-the-counter (OTC), compounded, or repackaged. Drives formulary tier assignment, cost-sharing rules, generic substitution logic, and rebate eligibility in PBM adjudication and formulary management.
reference: FDA Orange Book; FDA Purple Book (Biosimilars); CMS Part D; NCQA HEDIS Pharmacy Measures

description: The date on which this drug master record became effective and eligible for use in formulary configuration, PBM adjudication, and claims processing. Used for temporal validity enforcement in adjudication date-of-service lookups and formulary effective date management.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; Internal Formulary Management Policy

description: The current FDA regulatory approval status of the drug product. Approved drugs are eligible for formulary coverage. Tentatively approved generics may be covered under specific plan designs. Withdrawn or not-approved drugs are excluded from formulary and trigger claim denials. Required for CMS Part D formulary compliance.
reference: FDA Orange Book; FDA Purple Book; CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423

description: The International Nonproprietary Name (INN) or United States Adopted Name (USAN) for the active ingredient(s) of the drug (e.g., atorvastatin, adalimumab). Used for generic substitution logic, DUR screening, therapeutic equivalence grouping, and HEDIS pharmacy measure reporting.
reference: WHO INN Program; USAN Council; First Databank Drug Database

description: The 14-digit Medi-Span Generic Product Identifier (GPI) code providing a hierarchical drug classification from drug group (2 digits) through drug class, subclass, name, name extension, dosage form, and strength. Used as the primary therapeutic classification key in RxClaim/Argus PBM systems for formulary management, DUR screening, and rebate contracting.
reference: Medi-Span GPI Classification System; Wolters Kluwer Health Drug Database

description: Indicates whether this drug is clinically associated with one or more CMS Hierarchical Condition Categories (HCCs) for risk adjustment purposes. HCC-relevant drugs are used in RAF score modeling, RAPS/EDPS encounter data submissions, and population health stratification for Medicare Advantage plans.
reference: CMS HCC Risk Adjustment Model; CMS RAPS/EDPS Submission Requirements; 42 CFR Part 422

description: Indicates whether this drug is an FDA-approved biosimilar to a reference biological product. Biosimilars have distinct formulary placement rules, interchangeability designations, and rebate contracting considerations under CMS Part D and commercial plan designs.
reference: FDA Purple Book; Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA); CMS Part D Biosimilar Policy

description: Indicates whether an FDA-approved generic equivalent is available in the market for this brand-name drug. Used in formulary tier assignment, member cost-sharing communications, and generic substitution prompts during PBM adjudication and pharmacy dispensing.
reference: FDA Orange Book; CMS Part D Generic Substitution Policy; NCQA HEDIS PDC Measures

description: Indicates whether this drug is classified as a maintenance medication intended for long-term chronic condition management (e.g., antihypertensives, statins, diabetes medications). Maintenance drugs are eligible for 90-day supply dispensing at mail-order pharmacies and are used in HEDIS medication adherence measures (PDC).
reference: NCQA HEDIS Medication Adherence Measures; CMS Part D Medication Therapy Management (MTM) Criteria

description: Indicates whether this drug qualifies as a preventive medication under ACA Section 2713 or HDHP/HSA preventive care rules, making it eligible for $0 cost-sharing before the deductible is met. Used in benefit configuration and claims adjudication cost-sharing logic.
reference: ACA Section 2713; IRS Notice 2004-23 (HSA Preventive Care); USPSTF Preventive Drug List

description: Indicates whether this drug is classified as a specialty pharmaceutical requiring special handling, storage, administration, or monitoring (e.g., biologics, oncology agents, hepatitis C treatments). Specialty drugs are subject to mandatory specialty pharmacy channel requirements, prior authorization, and enhanced DUR in PBM adjudication. Critical for CMS Part D specialty tier placement.
reference: CMS Part D Specialty Tier Definition; NCPDP Specialty Drug Classification; PBM Specialty Drug List

description: The 5-digit FDA-assigned labeler code (first segment of the NDC) identifying the firm that manufactures, repackages, relabels, or distributes the drug. Used for manufacturer-level rebate aggregation and PBM contract management.
reference: FDA NDC Labeler Code Registry; CMS Part D

description: The FDA Orange Book multi-source code indicating the competitive market status of the drug: O=originator brand with no generic, M=multi-source (generic available), N=no current market (discontinued), Y=single-source generic. Used in generic substitution logic, formulary tier assignment, and MAC pricing eligibility determination.
reference: FDA Orange Book Multi-Source Code Definitions; CMS Part D Generic Substitution

description: The 11-digit National Drug Code assigned by the FDA uniquely identifying the labeler, product, and package size of a drug. This is the primary external business identifier for the drug and is used in pharmacy claims (NCPDP/837P), formulary management, PBM adjudication (RxClaim/Argus), and CMS Part D reporting. Stored in 5-4-2 format without hyphens.
reference: FDA National Drug Code Directory; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; CMS Part D Reporting Requirements

description: The NDC formatted in the standard 5-4-2 hyphenated display format (e.g., 12345-6789-01) as required for human-readable labeling, SBC documentation, and regulatory submissions to CMS and state DOIs.
reference: FDA NDC Labeling Requirements; CMS Part D Reporting

description: The quantity of drug units contained in the dispensed package as defined by the NDC (e.g., 30 tablets, 100 mL, 1 vial). Used in unit-of-use pricing calculations, days supply verification, quantity limit enforcement, and MAC pricing per-unit derivation.
reference: FDA NDC Package Size Definition; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; First Databank Drug Database

description: The unit of measure for the package size quantity (e.g., EA for each/tablet/capsule, ML for milliliter, GM for gram). Used in conjunction with package_size for accurate dispensing quantity calculations, days supply verification, and unit-cost pricing in PBM adjudication. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|ML|GM|MG|TAB|CAP|VIAL|PATCH|KIT — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; FDA NDC Package Size Terminology; First Databank Drug Database

description: The pharmacological mechanism-of-action category of the drug (e.g., ACE Inhibitor, Beta Blocker, SSRI, Statin, Monoclonal Antibody). Used for DUR drug-drug interaction screening, therapeutic duplication edits, clinical program targeting in care management, and HEDIS measure attribution.
reference: First Databank Drug Database; Medi-Span Drug Database; NCQA HEDIS Pharmacy Measures

business_glossary_term: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program
description: The name of the FDA-mandated Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program associated with this drug, if applicable (e.g., iPLEDGE for isotretinoin, TIRF REMS for fentanyl products). REMS drugs require special dispensing controls, patient enrollment, and prescriber certification that must be validated during PBM adjudication and prior authorization.
reference: FDA REMS Program Requirements (21 USC 355-1); FDA REMS Database

description: The path by which the drug is administered to the patient (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, topical, inhalation). Drives formulary benefit category assignment (medical vs. pharmacy benefit), prior authorization requirements, and specialty pharmacy routing in PBM adjudication. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|ophthalmic|otic|rectal — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA Route of Administration Terminology; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard; First Databank Drug Database

description: The native record identifier from the originating source system (First Databank, Medi-Span, RxClaim, or Argus) for this drug master record. Used for data lineage, cross-system reconciliation, and upstream change tracking in the lakehouse ingestion pipeline.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164)

description: Identifies the operational source system from which this drug master record was ingested (e.g., FDB=First Databank, MEDISPAN=Medi-Span, RXCLAIM=RxClaim PBM, ARGUS=Argus PBM, INTERNAL=internally maintained). Used for data lineage tracking, conflict resolution during ETL, and audit compliance in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164); SOC 2 Data Lineage Requirements

description: The concentration or potency of the active ingredient(s) expressed as a numeric value with unit of measure (e.g., 10 mg, 500 mg/5 mL, 0.25%). Used in DUR duplicate therapy screening, quantity limit enforcement, and clinical appropriateness review in UM/PA workflows.
reference: FDA Drug Labeling Requirements; First Databank Drug Database; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard

description: The date on which this drug master record was terminated or superseded, indicating the drug is no longer active for formulary placement or new claim adjudication. Null indicates the record is currently active. Used for historical claims repricing and formulary audit trails.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; Internal Formulary Management Policy

description: The standardized code identifying the broad therapeutic class of the drug (e.g., cardiovascular agents, anti-infectives, antineoplastics). Used for formulary tier grouping, rebate contract aggregation, utilization reporting, and disease management program enrollment triggers.
reference: First Databank Enhanced Therapeutic Classification (ETC); Medi-Span GPI Therapeutic Classification

description: The human-readable name of the therapeutic class corresponding to the therapeutic_class_code. Used in formulary displays, member-facing SBC documents, provider communications, and regulatory reporting to CMS and state DOIs.
reference: First Databank Enhanced Therapeutic Classification (ETC); Medi-Span GPI Therapeutic Classification

description: The FDA Orange Book therapeutic equivalence evaluation code (e.g., AB, AA, BC) indicating whether a generic drug is therapeutically equivalent to the reference listed drug. AB-rated generics are substitutable at the pharmacy. Used in generic substitution logic, formulary step therapy, and DAW (Dispense As Written) override processing in PBM adjudication.
reference: FDA Orange Book (Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations); 21 CFR Part 314

description: The standardized code identifying the therapeutic subclass within the broader therapeutic class (e.g., HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors within cardiovascular agents). Enables granular formulary tier differentiation, step therapy protocol design, and rebate contract segmentation.
reference: First Databank Enhanced Therapeutic Classification (ETC); Medi-Span GPI Therapeutic Classification

description: The human-readable name of the therapeutic subclass corresponding to the therapeutic_subclass_code. Used in formulary management workflows, clinical program configuration, and detailed utilization analytics.
reference: First Databank Enhanced Therapeutic Classification (ETC); Medi-Span GPI Therapeutic Classification

description: The timestamp when this drug master record was last modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Used for incremental data refresh, change detection, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks lakehouse pipeline.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164.312); SOC 2 Audit Trail Requirements; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: The Wholesale Acquisition Cost (WAC) per unit as reported by the manufacturer, representing the list price to wholesalers before discounts and rebates. Used as a pricing benchmark for specialty drug reimbursement, rebate baseline calculations, and CMS Part D coverage gap discount program calculations.
reference: 42 USC 1395w-3a (WAC Definition); CMS Part D Coverage Gap Discount Program; Medi-Span WAC

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each NDC-level drug pricing record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the drug_pricing data product.

Foreign key linking to pharmacy.drug_master. Business justification: drug_pricing records are defined per NDC; linking to drug_master provides the authoritative drug attributes and eliminates duplicated columns.

Percentage discount applied to AWP to derive the reimbursement rate under AWP-based contracts (e.g., AWP minus 15%). Expressed as a positive decimal percentage (e.g., 15.0000 = 15%). Used for PBM contract compliance validation and reimbursement audits.
reference: PBM Contract Terms; CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual

description: Average Wholesale Price per unit as published by First Databank or Medi-Span. Commonly used as the benchmark for pharmacy reimbursement calculations and discount negotiations. Expressed in USD.
reference: First Databank (FDB); Medi-Span Price Rx; CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual

description: Timestamp when this drug pricing record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and SLA monitoring of pricing file processing.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164)

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary price fields in this record (e.g., USD). Supports multi-currency operations for Puerto Rico and other US territories. Defaults to USD for domestic plans.
Number of days of drug supply for which this pricing record applies (e.g., 30-day retail, 90-day mail order). Used to differentiate pricing tiers by supply duration per PBM contract terms.
reference: PBM Contract Terms; CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual

description: DEA controlled substance schedule classification (CI through CV) or NON-CONTROLLED. Used for DUR edits, quantity limit enforcement, prior authorization requirements, and regulatory compliance reporting.
reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act (21 USC 812); 21 CFR Part 1308

description: Pharmacy dispensing channel for which this pricing record applies: retail (community pharmacy), mail_order (90-day supply mail service), specialty (specialty pharmacy), or long_term_care (LTC facility pharmacy). Pricing may differ by channel per PBM contract terms.
reference: PBM Contract Terms; CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual

description: Fixed dispensing fee in USD paid to the pharmacy per prescription fill, separate from the ingredient cost. Defined in PBM network contracts and applied during claim adjudication to calculate total pharmacy reimbursement.
reference: PBM Contract Terms; CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual

description: Date on which this pricing record becomes effective and applicable for claim adjudication. Used to select the correct price for a claim based on the date of service. Aligns with PBM pricing file effective dates.
reference: CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual; PBM Contract Terms

description: Date on which this pricing record expires and is no longer applicable for new claim adjudication. Null indicates an open-ended pricing record with no defined end date. Used with effective_date to determine the active pricing window.
reference: CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual; PBM Contract Terms

description: Formulary tier assignment for this drug under the applicable plan benefit design (e.g., tier_1=preferred generic, tier_2=generic, tier_3=preferred brand, tier_4=non-preferred brand, tier_5=specialty). Drives member cost-sharing (copay/coinsurance) during claim adjudication.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Guidelines; NCQA Standards; ACA Essential Health Benefits

description: Version identifier of the MAC list, used to track updates and revisions to the MAC pricing schedule. Supports audit trails for MAC list changes and pharmacy reimbursement disputes. Null when price_type is not MAC.
reference: CMS Part D MAC Policy; PBM Contract Terms

description: Describes the methodology used to derive the MAC price (e.g., MARKET_BASKET=based on market survey of acquisition costs, NADAC_BASED=derived from CMS NADAC data, AWP_DISCOUNT=percentage discount from AWP, WAC_DISCOUNT=percentage discount from WAC, CUSTOM=plan-specific methodology). Required for PBM contract compliance and regulatory transparency. Null when price_type is not MAC.
reference: CMS Part D MAC Policy; NAIC Model Pharmacy Benefit Law

description: Maximum Allowable Cost per unit set by the PBM or health plan for generic and multi-source drugs. Represents the upper reimbursement limit for a drug under the applicable MAC list. Expressed in USD. Null when price_type is not MAC.
reference: CMS Part D MAC Policy; NAIC Model Pharmacy Benefit Law; PBM Contract Terms

description: FDA Orange Book multi-source code indicating the competitive market status of the drug: O=Originator brand (no generic), M=Multi-source (generic available), N=Non-multi-source, Y=Generic product. Used to determine MAC eligibility and generic substitution applicability.
reference: FDA Orange Book; First Databank (FDB); CMS Part D MAC Policy

description: Quantity of units contained in the standard package as defined by the NDC. Used to convert between package-level and per-unit pricing and to validate dispensed quantity against package size during adjudication.
reference: FDA National Drug Code Directory; First Databank (FDB)

description: Unit of measure for the package size quantity (e.g., TAB for tablets, ML for milliliters). Distinct from unit_of_measure which applies to the pricing unit; this field describes the package-level quantity unit. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|ML|GM|MG|UN|TAB|CAP|VIAL|PATCH — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA National Drug Code Directory; NCPDP SCRIPT Standard

description: Percentage change in unit price from the prior pricing record to the current record, calculated as ((unit_price - prior_unit_price) / prior_unit_price) * 100. Used for drug price inflation monitoring, CMS price increase reporting, and PBM contract compliance.
reference: CMS Drug Pricing Transparency; Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) Drug Pricing Provisions

description: Classifies the pricing methodology represented by this record: AWP (Average Wholesale Price), WAC (Wholesale Acquisition Cost), MAC (Maximum Allowable Cost), RBP (Reference Based Pricing), NADAC (National Average Drug Acquisition Cost), or Usual and Customary. Determines how the price is applied during claim adjudication and reimbursement calculation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: AWP|WAC|MAC|RBP|NADAC|USUAL_AND_CUSTOMARY — promote to reference product]
reference: CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual; NAIC Model Pharmacy Benefit Law

description: Publication or release date of the source pricing file from which this record was extracted. Used to track pricing file currency, identify stale pricing data, and support audit and reconciliation processes.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; PBM Contract Terms

description: Name of the source pricing file from which this record was loaded (e.g., 'FDB_PRICE_20240101.txt', 'RXCLAIM_MAC_Q1_2024.csv'). Used for data lineage, audit trails, and troubleshooting pricing discrepancies.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; PBM Contract Terms

description: Identifies the originating source of the pricing data (e.g., First Databank, Medi-Span, RxClaim PBM feed, Argus PBM feed, CMS published rates, internal custom pricing). Critical for audit trails and PBM contract compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDB|MEDISPAN|RXCLAIM|ARGUS|CMS|INTERNAL|CUSTOM — promote to reference product]
reference: PBM Contract Terms; CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual

description: Current lifecycle status of the pricing record: active (currently in use for adjudication), inactive (no longer applicable), pending (approved but not yet effective), superseded (replaced by a newer pricing record for the same NDC and price type).
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; PBM Contract Terms

description: Previous per-unit price for this NDC and price type before the most recent pricing update. Used for price change analysis, trend reporting, and PBM contract compliance audits.
reference: PBM Contract Terms; Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Reference Based Pricing per unit used as the benchmark reimbursement amount under RBP pharmacy contracts. Expressed in USD. Null when price_type is not RBP.
reference: PBM Contract Terms; ERISA Plan Design

description: Dispensing unit of measure for which the price applies (e.g., EA=Each, ML=Milliliter, GM=Gram, MG=Milligram, UN=Unit, TAB=Tablet, CAP=Capsule, VIAL=Vial, PATCH=Patch). Required for accurate per-unit cost calculation during adjudication. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|ML|GM|MG|UN|TAB|CAP|VIAL|PATCH — promote to reference product]

Per-unit drug price expressed in USD for the applicable price type (AWP, WAC, MAC, or RBP). Used as the basis for claim adjudication, cost-sharing calculation, and pharmacy reimbursement. Precision to 6 decimal places to accommodate high-precision specialty drug pricing.
reference: CMS Part D Prescription Drug Benefit Manual; PBM Contract Terms

description: Timestamp when this drug pricing record was last modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for change data capture (CDC), incremental processing, and audit trail maintenance.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164)

description: Wholesale Acquisition Cost per unit as reported by the manufacturer to the pricing compendia. Represents the list price from manufacturer to wholesaler before discounts. Expressed in USD. Used in WAC-based reimbursement contracts.
reference: 42 USC 1395w-3a; First Databank (FDB); Medi-Span Price Rx

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the formulary record. Primary key for the formulary data product in the pharmacy domain.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; HIPAA Administrative Simplification

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Formulary design must adhere to specific regulatory obligations (ACA, CMS); linking enables reporting of compliance status per formulary.
Reference to the immediately preceding version of this formulary. Enables formulary change tracking, member notification workflows, and historical adjudication lookups for appeals and grievances.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Change Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120(b)

description: Business classification of the formulary indicating its benefit richness level relative to other formularies offered by the plan. Used in benefit design analytics, member communications, and plan comparison tools.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Design Guidelines; NCQA Accreditation Standards; ACA SBC Requirements

description: Date on which member notification was sent for formulary changes. CMS Part D requires 60-day advance notice for non-preferred formulary changes and immediate notification for safety-related removals.
reference: CMS Part D 42 CFR Part 423.120(b)(3); CMS Member Notification Requirements

business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Formulary Identifier
description: The CMS-assigned formulary identifier used in Part D formulary file submissions to CMS. Required for Medicare Part D plans to identify the formulary in RAPS and EDPS submissions.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary File Submission; 42 CFR Part 423; CMS HPMS Formulary Submission Guidelines

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the formulary across systems, used in EDI transactions, PBM interfaces, and CMS Part D submissions. Corresponds to the formulary ID field in RxClaim/Argus PBM system.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary File Submission Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423

description: Timestamp when this formulary record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance documentation purposes.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR Part 164; Enterprise Data Governance Audit Requirements

description: Free-text business description of the formulary, including its intended population, key design features, and any notable coverage inclusions or exclusions. Used in internal documentation and plan benefit configuration.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Documentation Requirements; NCQA Accreditation Standards

description: Total number of unique drug entries (NDC or drug-tier combinations) included in this formulary at the time of the last update. Used for formulary adequacy assessments and CMS Part D formulary file validation.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Adequacy Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120; CMS Formulary File Submission

description: Indicates whether Drug Utilization Review (DUR) edits are applied during adjudication under this formulary. DUR programs screen for drug interactions, duplicate therapy, and inappropriate dosing per OBRA '90 requirements.
reference: OBRA '90 DUR Requirements; CMS Part D DUR Program; 42 CFR Part 423.153; NCQA Pharmacy Standards

description: The date on which this formulary becomes active and applicable to member benefit adjudication. Used by PBM systems (RxClaim/Argus) to determine which formulary version applies at point of dispensing.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120

description: Current lifecycle status of the formulary record. Active formularies are used in live adjudication; pending formularies are approved but not yet effective; retired formularies are historical records no longer in use.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; NCQA Accreditation Standards

description: Classification of the formulary structure indicating coverage breadth and tier design. Open formularies cover most drugs; closed formularies restrict to listed drugs only; tiered formularies apply differential cost-sharing by tier.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; NCQA Pharmacy Benefit Standards

description: Policy governing generic drug substitution at point of dispensing. Mandatory substitution requires dispensing of generic equivalents; permissive allows brand if requested; DAW (Dispense As Written) honored respects prescriber instructions.
reference: State Pharmacy Practice Acts; CMS Part D Generic Substitution Requirements; NCQA Pharmacy Standards

description: Indicates whether this formulary meets ACA Qualified Health Plan (QHP) essential health benefit (EHB) drug coverage requirements, including the required drug categories and classes under 45 CFR Part 156.
reference: ACA 45 CFR Part 156; CMS QHP Formulary Requirements; HHS EHB Benchmark Plan

business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Part D Indicator
description: Indicates whether this formulary is subject to CMS Medicare Part D regulatory requirements, including annual bid submission, formulary file submission to CMS, and coverage determination obligations.
reference: CMS Part D; 42 CFR Part 423; Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual

description: Date on which the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee last reviewed and approved this formulary. P&T Committee review is required for CMS Part D compliance and NCQA accreditation.
reference: CMS Part D P&T Committee Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120(b)(1); NCQA Accreditation Standards

description: Line of Business (LOB) associated with this formulary, indicating the regulatory and market segment under which the formulary operates. Drives CMS Part D, Medicaid, or commercial compliance requirements.
reference: CMS Part D 42 CFR Part 423; CMS Medicaid Drug Rebate Program; ACA QHP Requirements

description: Indicates whether this formulary is designated for use by Low Income Subsidy (LIS) eligible members under Medicare Part D. LIS formularies must meet CMS benchmark plan requirements for cost-sharing and drug coverage.
reference: CMS Part D LIS Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.780; CMS Low Income Subsidy Program

description: Indicates whether this formulary supports mail-order pharmacy dispensing. Mail-order programs typically offer 90-day supplies at reduced cost-sharing and are a key component of pharmacy benefit design.
reference: CMS Part D Mail Order Requirements; NCQA Pharmacy Benefit Standards; State Mail Order Pharmacy Laws

description: Human-readable business name of the formulary (e.g., 'Standard Commercial Formulary 2025', 'Medicare Part D Enhanced Formulary'). Used in member-facing materials, SBC documents, and plan benefit configurations.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; NCQA Accreditation Standards

description: Scheduled date for the next Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee review of this formulary. Supports compliance tracking for CMS Part D requirements mandating regular formulary review cycles.
reference: CMS Part D P&T Committee Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120(b)(1); NCQA Accreditation Standards

description: The formulary identifier as assigned by the PBM system (RxClaim or Argus). Used for cross-system reconciliation between the health plan's internal formulary record and the PBM's formulary configuration.
reference: RxClaim Formulary Management Module; Argus PBM System

description: The benefit plan year (e.g., 2025) for which this formulary is effective. Used for annual formulary change management, CMS Part D annual bid submissions, and benefit year reporting.
reference: CMS Part D Annual Bid Submission; 45 CFR Part 156 ACA QHP Requirements

description: Indicates whether this formulary requires prior authorization (PA) for any covered drugs. PA requirements are subject to CMS Part D coverage determination timelines and member appeal rights.
reference: CMS Part D Prior Authorization Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.578; CMS Coverage Determination Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee Approval Date
description: Date on which the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee formally approved this formulary or the most recent formulary update. Required documentation for CMS Part D compliance and NCQA accreditation audits.
reference: CMS Part D P&T Committee Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120(b)(1); NCQA HP Accreditation Standards

description: Indicates whether this formulary applies quantity limits (QL) on covered drugs, restricting the amount dispensed per fill or per defined time period. Quantity limits are a utilization management tool subject to CMS Part D exception requirements.
reference: CMS Part D Quantity Limit Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.578; CMS Coverage Determination Guidelines

description: The date on which CMS or the applicable State Department of Insurance approved this formulary for use. Required for Part D compliance documentation and audit trails.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Approval; 42 CFR Part 423; State DOI Approval Process

description: The date on which the formulary was submitted to CMS or the applicable State Department of Insurance for regulatory review and approval.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Submission Deadlines; 42 CFR Part 423; State DOI Filing Requirements

description: Status of the formulary's regulatory filing with CMS or applicable State Department of Insurance (DOI). Tracks whether the formulary has been submitted, approved, or rejected for compliance with Part D or state market requirements.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Submission; 42 CFR Part 423; State DOI Filing Requirements; NAIC Model Laws

description: Identifies the operational source system from which this formulary record originated (e.g., RxClaim, Argus PBM system, Facets). Used for data lineage tracking and cross-system reconciliation in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: Enterprise Data Governance Standards; HIPAA Administrative Simplification

description: Indicates whether this formulary designates a specialty pharmacy network for dispensing high-cost specialty drugs. Specialty pharmacy programs may include limited distribution networks and enhanced clinical support services.
reference: CMS Part D Specialty Pharmacy Requirements; URAC Specialty Pharmacy Accreditation; NCQA Pharmacy Standards

description: Indicates whether this formulary includes a specialty drug tier for high-cost specialty medications. Specialty tiers typically apply to drugs with monthly costs exceeding CMS specialty tier threshold (currently $670/month for Part D).
reference: CMS Part D Specialty Tier Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.578; CMS HPMS Formulary Guidance

description: Indicates whether this formulary employs step therapy (also known as fail-first) protocols requiring members to try lower-cost or preferred drugs before coverage of higher-cost alternatives is authorized.
reference: CMS Part D Step Therapy Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423; State Step Therapy Laws; URAC Utilization Management Standards

description: The date on which this formulary is no longer active. Null indicates an open-ended formulary with no defined end date. Used for formulary version management and historical adjudication lookups.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120

description: The total number of cost-sharing tiers defined in this formulary (e.g., 3-tier, 4-tier, 5-tier, 6-tier). Determines the tier structure used in drug tier assignments and member cost-sharing calculations.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Requirements; NCQA Pharmacy Benefit Standards

description: Timestamp when this formulary record was last modified. Used for change tracking, incremental data loads in the Databricks Silver layer, and audit trail requirements.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR Part 164; Enterprise Data Governance Audit Requirements

description: Public-facing URL where members can access the formulary drug list. CMS Part D and ACA QHP regulations require health plans to publish formularies online and provide the URL in plan materials and SBC documents.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Transparency Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.128; ACA 45 CFR Part 156.230; SBC Requirements

description: Version number of the formulary, incremented with each approved update or mid-year formulary change. Used to track formulary change history and ensure members receive required 60-day advance notice of non-preferred changes.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary Change Requirements; 42 CFR Part 423.120(b); NCQA Accreditation Standards

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each formulary drug tier assignment record. Primary key for this association entity linking a drug (NDC) to a formulary with its tier, cost-sharing, and utilization management (UM) controls.
reference: CMS Part D Formulary File Submission Requirements; HIPAA EDI Standards

description: Foreign key linking to utilization.clinical_criteria. Business justification: Formulary drug tier PA criteria and step therapy clinical rationale are defined by clinical criteria records. pa_criteria_description and st_clinical_rationale are denormalized text representations of
